newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper weaker, all eyes on LME spreads.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper weaker, all eyes on LME spreads.

text.p: COMEX copper opened higher before moving lower in choppy early trading, as the market kept a close eye on the surging nearby spreads on LME.

"COMEX is choppy in line with London. It seems like a lot of the players are standing away from the market," Malcolm Freeman of GNI Ltd said. "People are just order executing and the market has become extremely nervous."
At 0957 EDT September COMEX copper was off 1.50 cents at 104.80 cents a lb, traded 106.90 to 104.80 cents. Spot July was down 1.70 cents at 108.50 cents.

LME backwardation which doubled to a high of about $270 on Monday, eased back to $235/$250 after COMEX opened Tuesday, but the very nearby spreads strengthened to just shy of the limit imposed by the exchange.
Some dealers expected the tightness on LME to last until the end of July, helping to suck metal from COMEX depots to their LME counterparts in the U.S.
LME stocks rose 2,100 tonnes Tuesday to 143,300 tonnes, while COMEX stocks Monday fell sharply by 2,379 short tons to 33,075 tons.
